prompt:
How the hell do I stay focused when studying? This is legitimately my last chance at not ending up like a fucking loser with no future and I still can't bring myself to study appropriately to do so.

I've changed programs a couple times, I'm two years behind. I finally got into the program of my choice (Computer Science) and now all I need to do is actually get it done.

I have such a hard time staying focused on classes that don't interest me. I like coding, so when I take those classes I do we
response:
Go to a "studious" place to study, like your university library or a public library study room. This will semi-jolt you into at least having half a go at studying.

When you sit down at your study place, write a to-do list, and break down the boring subjects into bite-sized achievable tasks. 

ie. 
- Read 1 page of subject x and write a one or two sentence summary of what it was about in your own words.
- Repeat above 5 times, then change subjects unless you're suddenly in the vibe of that subject and are inspired to continue
- Write terms next to their definitions, then chop them up, rearrange them and match them back together to test yourself.

Write a list of about 10 items and for every 3 you tick off, reward yourself with some time on your phone...set a 10 minute timer to remind you to put your phone down and get back to study.

Good luck

How to deal with people whom you haven't spoken to in several years and they need need your help. Hey guys, I always read the lovely LPTs that you guys post and trust me, they have helped me a lot. Thank you!

response:
In part, it depends on the request. You should be suspicious, especially if the request is for money or to sell you something. 

I decline requests for money.... in my experience, people who cannot get their shit together financially will screw you over. If they are calling you after all these years, they've burned all their other bridges. 

Selling me something...... sometimes its worth a listen, if the person has started a business selling something I might need in future, like financial services, insurance, real estate etc... it can't hurt to have the contact if they are reputable. But beware of anything that sounds odd or outlandish or unprofessional. if so they have some kind of angle where you'll lose. 

On occasion I have received such requests simply for advice, including a request for a letter of reference, advice on what car (new or used) to buy, or a request for mentoring if they are starting a business or career. I usually provide assistance, because it won't me anything except a bit of time and I can gain a helpful professional or personal contact.

prompt:
We are both from the city. Lately I've been thinking about the state of economy (trending down) and uncertainty of the future, and I want to make as much money as I can while I'm still young and healthy. I also want to use the capital to start a business in my early 30s. 

However my girlfriend is obviously not keen on the idea, due to the long distance (at least 3hrs to an airport hub then another 2hrs on a regional plane that only flies semi regularly and at exorbitant fees, and not at all dur
response:
I mean, it's a tough one. I did long distance for several years and while I've got no regrets about it, I also don't recommend it to anyone....especially if they can help it. LDRs, especially ones with logistical issues like yours would have, are tough as nails to get through. This is especially the case when you're talking years or more. 

Unfortunately, there's not really any advice about it other than emphasizing the importance of communication, transparency, and empathy. You have to work extra hard to prioritize the relationship over all else during this if you want it to work...to the point it heavily effects every part of your life. 

It's entirely possible, and frankly reasonable, that your GF just doesn't want to go through that, or that even if it works for a little while, it just falls apart for one reason or another...none of which is really anyone's fault. Basically, what I'm saying is be prepared for this to not work out.

I'd also throw a bit of additional caution in because moving from Big City to Remote Rural Mining town is a HUGE culture shock. HUGE. That alone could be enough to unravel this whole thing.

prompt:
This is a tough one and I've no idea how to formalize my thoughts. I'll be visiting a therapist next week but I desperately want to talk with someone about it. I tried using logic, tried using emotions, but I can't figure out if I'm sabotaging myself or if there's actually something there.

Me and my girlfriend have been together for little over 2 years. She recently moved in, some half a year ago. There's really nothing wrong with our relationship: we never fight, rarely argue, we deeply care a
response:
You've said it yourself, you're both busy with work and haven't been on a date in a while. Honestly, sometimes I also have phases like you have right now. But I always found that this was due to a breakdown in honest communication and attention. When I shared my feelings about what's been bothering me with my partner, then I'd feel much closer again. Same with when we put in more effort to see each other. I choose to stay with him and he chooses to stay with me - and that's why we can come back from times of emotional distance. 

A relationship is work, and if you don't put in the work, then it deteriorates and gets stale. 
You've said it yourself, you don't find anything wrong with her and you even see yourself longterm with her. Yes, there is probably a person out there who's more compatible with you or who could make you even happier. But the "chasing" Mindset isn't exactly known for leading to healthy and full filled relationships since people rarely turn it off once they've found someone new. The grass could be greener, but unless you know why you feel like your grass isn't green enough, you'll never find someone who matches the more greener grass you've envisioned.

You don't have to stick it out if you continue to feel like this AFTER you've put in the work, but I'd highly recommend that you give it a try, talk to her about your feelings and set up some date nights with her before you decide. 
And write out what makes you feel annoyed and frustrated, and talk to her about these things. She can't change what she isn't aware off. Good luck!
